name: potemkin
description: Composable, language-agnostic type pretty-printing for your language servers (rust-analyzer, clangd, gopls, and more) via the Potemkin LSP proxy.

potemkin.enabled.description: Automatically wrap detected language servers with the Potemkin proxy on activation.

potemkin.servers.markdownDescription: Additional language servers to wrap, beyond the built-ins (rust-analyzer, clangd, gopls). Each entry describes how to override that server's binary.

extensionId.description: Owning VS Code extension id, used for auto-detection (optional).

pathSetting.description: Dotted config path whose value overrides the server binary, e.g. "clangd.path".

pathSettingField.description: If pathSetting is an object, the field within it holding the server path (e.g. "gopls").

restartCommand.description: Command id that restarts the server after its path changes.

defaultCommand.description: Real server command to wrap when no explicit path is configured.

languages.description: LSP languageIds this server handles (e.g. ["rust"]). Forwarded as POTEMKIN_LANGUAGES so only matching-language plugins load.

potemkin.unicode.description: Allow unicode symbols in pretty-printed output (POTEMKIN_UNICODE).

potemkin.pluginsDir.description: Optional extra directory of plugin manifests, searched *before* the extension-managed dir (used by companion extensions) and Potemkin's default (~/.config/potemkin/plugins). Leave empty unless you hand-maintain manifests.

potemkin.pluginOrder.markdownDescription:
Explicit application order for plugins (POTEMKIN_PLUGIN_ORDER), earliest first. When several plugins rewrite the same hover/inlay text they run as a chain, each seeing the previous plugin's output, so order matters for *layered* rendering — e.g. list `nholthaus-units` before `typed-linear-algebra` so element unit types are prettified before the matrix pretty-printer wraps them.

List plugin ids (the manifest `name`). Listed plugins run first, in this order; unlisted plugins follow, ordered by their manifest `order` then name. Overrides each plugin's manifest `order`. Leave empty to use the authors' declared ordering.

potemkin.pluginTimeoutMs.markdownDescription: Default per-plugin timeout in milliseconds (POTEMKIN_PLUGIN_TIMEOUT_MS) for a single `initialize`/`transform` round trip. If a plugin exceeds it, Potemkin kills that plugin and drops it for the session — its text passes through untouched — so a hung or pathologically slow plugin can never stall a hover or inlay hint. A plugin's own manifest `timeout_ms` overrides this. Leave at `0` to use Potemkin's built-in default (5000 ms).

potemkin.multiplex.markdownDescription: Enable per-directory language-server configuration (POTEMKIN_MULTIPLEX). **Last resort:** when on, Potemkin runs a separate backend process for each subtree whose `potemkin.toml` overrides the server's settings, so different directories get genuinely different config. This is heavier than a single session (each backend indexes its view of the tree) and is only needed for servers that can't do this themselves. Off by default; the common path is a transparent single-backend proxy.

potemkin.raw.markdownDescription:
Per-language-server rendering of the **Raw:** section that Potemkin appends below a pretty-printed hover (showing the original, pre-transform type). This is a property of the *server's* hover format, so it is configured per server rather than per plugin.

Keys are server ids (`rust-analyzer`, `clangd`, `gopls`, or a custom server id). Each value may set:
- `enabled` (boolean) — show the section at all.
- `label` (string) — header text, e.g. `"Raw:"` (empty to omit).
- `fence` (string) — a code-fence language such as `"rust"` for markdown hovers; use `""` for plaintext hovers (e.g. clangd's).
- `separator` (boolean) — prepend a `---` rule.

Omitted keys/fields fall back to sensible built-in defaults (markdown + `rust`/`go` fence for rust-analyzer/gopls; plaintext for clangd).

enabled.description: Show the Raw: section for this server.

label.description: Header text above the raw type (empty to omit).

fence.description: Code-fence language for the raw body (e.g. "rust"); empty for plaintext hovers.

separator.description: Prepend a markdown --- rule before the section.
